Bedwyr 0 lethality (+1) due to deathmark. Princeps +1 lethality +1 longevity and +1 utility due to it being damage dealer with TNA and 2 alpha 2 beta as well as the force push ability that can CC enemies. -3 accessibility due to it being paid gambling only, so overall same grade. Atlas utility +1 mobility +1 due to jump, accessibility -2 for same reason. 
Bjorn +1 lethality, it has an entire alpha weapon on most brawlers. Added Kid, Ming, Arthur. Kaji 0 longevity, nondens 0 longevity. -Adazahi

After a bit of discussion through discord, Crisis deserves +1 mobility if Bagliore has +1 for having a simple relatively one-time use beacon teleport (which should be used defensively instead of for covering ground, but that's neither here nor there) -Tropical
Skyros +2 mobility -1 lethality to be consistent with Loki -Adazahi changed adazahi password and signed him out of his account have fun 😂-tropical
Blitz utility +1, access 0, since it has suppression but still relies on statchecking when the suppression runs out (or if the enemy has anticontrol). also, blew up tropical's house. -adzadongy

Bot re-evaluations: Crisis mobility +1->0, Bagliore mobility +1->0, accessibility -2->-1, Ravager accessibility +1->0, Dux Longevity 0->+1 Mobility +1->0.
Footnote: Considering re-evaluation of accessibility ratings for Sword-Unit and Teth. Let this also be a reminder that the point of rating things systematically is that the process should determine the results, not the other way around.
Mobility is most certainly not a category Crisis excels in. Lethality and Accessibility should be the two areas where a debate can be had. 
An argument that either Flux/Gauss Crisis is a legitimate build or that Crisis should have +2 Lethality would be still lukewarm, but significantly more tenable than Crisis being a mobility king. - Mistermath
Math and I decided on Crisis, Stryx, and Bagliore all sharing +2 lethality as they are the three highest firepower piercer-holders in the game, and unlike behemoth, the only other 4H bot, also have either damage boosts or 5H. -Adazahi
Bot re-evaluations: Teth & Sword Unit Accessibility -1 -> 0. - Mistermath

Bot re-evaluations: Blitz Utility +1->0. Moved back down to bring in line with other suppression robots. Consider raising Rayker from 0 to +1 in the future due to significantly more range and charges on suppression. - Mistermath
Bot re-evaluations: Ravager Longevity 0->+1. Bringing in line with Loki and Crisis. Worth noting that Ravager's superior bulk to Crisis may allow it to act as a slower Loki. -Mistermath

Bot re-evaluations: Fury Utility +1->-1, Accessibility +1->+2. Jaeger mobility -1->0. Changes for the purposes of consistency. In terms of accessibility, Fury is the only pre-leveled T3 bot. -Mistermath
Added Ammit at a total rating of +2. -adazi
Changed sword description to remove anything about execute. It's execution threshold is too low to reliably execute things anymore - Adazahi
Added new "Bot Roles" page. -Mistermath & Adazahi

Edited the Nuo & Lio short blurbs to exclude the "available through common data pads" part, and increased Hastatus's accessibility rating to -1 from -2. At least, with Kaji being at -1 and 
Hastatus also being in the same pads & locations as Kaji, I think it's fair to have it at -1. Also somewhat of the same reasoning as to why Bagliore has -1 in accessibility. 
Maybe considering increasing Rex's accessibility to -2 from -3? My reasoning being Bull isn't mandatory (personally ran it long enough to determine that mk3 is the bigger & more impactful hurdle), 
and the fact Ammit h-as -2 despite being economically the same as Rex was on its release. -Tropical

Edited Nuo & Lio comments to mention expected future additions to superchest in order to justify maintaining accessibility rating. Fixed what appeared to be a consistency error for Orochi and Nether on T4 tab. - Mistermath
Started progress on mini build guides. Added info about roles and mini build guides section to the intro. - Adazahi
Finished mini build guide. -adazahi
Added hastatus build guide, removed titan chargers, devourer 0->+1 utility and +1->0 longevity, edited descriptions for Bjorn, Devourer, and Princeps - Adazahi
Removed ARM from pathfinder build guide. % damage weapons dont scale well with hunter stacks. Added pretty colors for organization. -Adazahi
Update for 11.8 patch: Lio longevity +2->+1. Corrected utility for Rex/Hastatus from 0->-1. -Mistermath
Added Anaskor, gradually working on rating changes for other Robots due to rebalance wave. -Tropical

Ankasor lethality +2 -> +1. While Ankasor sports decent firepower and a really good BiW, it's seemingly insane firepower is carried by the OP new guns, which the other +2 Lethality bots (ie Bagliore) can wield many more of. -Adazahi

Kaji mobility 1 -> 0, Access -1 -> 0. Nerfs really reduced it's speed, but it's in common data pads now. Rex Longevity 2 -> 1, Access -3 -> 2. Rex isn't as tanky as before, but it's a little easier to get your hands on now. 
Princeps access -3 -> -2, Atlas access -2 -> -1, both are & have been inside the titan pads for a few months now. Sword mobility 1 -> 0, don't use the dash anymore, utility -1 -> 0, run it like a siren with lockdown unit. 
Updated a few robot & titan comments, roles, and mini build guides as well. -Adazahi & Tropical
Re-evaluated what counts as 2 mobility. Imugi, Nightingale, Strider, Nuo, Raven, Nether, and Seraph all have been raised from 1 -> 2. -Adazahi
Changed pilot recommendation on Skirmisher Anaksor to Mei Lan -Adazahi

Added UE Devastator + UE Havoc to Anaksor titan slayer build suggestions. Eiffel and Bersagliere Mobility changed from 1 -> 2 to fit with new mobility evaluation standards. Dagon access changed from -2 -> -1 because while it requires 6 weapons and statchecks, it's available through black market. Stryx, who is available through only data pads and still requires 5 weapons is only -1, so this seems fair. -Adazahi
Changed f2p Imugi mini build guide reccomendation to Growler Howler from Havoc Scatter. -Adazahi

Changed mini build guide weapons: Dux best -> replaced any ue weapons with close range only, Demeter best -> replaced any UE weapons with close range only, Lio f2p -> Growler, Leech f2p -> growler + porthos, 
Nuo best -> Machiara + Basilus or UE redeemer/taran, Lynx f2p -> Nucleon or Talon, Siren -> renamed "titan charger" to "titan charger/assault", Raptor best -> close range UE or kroko guns, Nightingale best -> Elox Murix, 
UE burst weapons, Kroko guns, Teth best -> removed hybrid acid shotgun build, Ammit -> Added machiara + velios and close range UE to best, rust rocket, bsg, and growler to f2p, Raven best -> added midrange UE setups, Anaksor f2p -> added screamer growler
re-added pilum + gladius to all midrange setups that had it entirely replaced with anaksor guns, the extra 100m of range makes it a decent option (though still mostly worse than anaksor guns, still best at 600m). Added UE index, added rust machine guns to any bots with atomizer or nucleon suggested.
-Adazahi

Re-evaluations: Samjok Access 0 -> +1, Anaksor Access -2 -> -3. Samjok is in the gold chest and doesn't require much leveling to function. Anaksor without the drone has issues with chip damage. -Adazahi
Added Vector & Waymaker. -Tropical. Added Vector to mini build guides + edited anaksor best pilot to be the new one. -Adazahi
Added new curving flames to mini build guides. -Adazahi Fixed the way adazahi credits his notes in the changes log -Tropical
Re-evaluations: Bulgasari mobility 0 -> +1, Haechi mobility 0 -> +1. Multiple dashes are now sufficient for +1 rating. Rex accessibility -2 -> -1 following move to common/blue pads. -Mistermath
Changed F2P builds for Loki and Skyros (beacon capper) to harpoons. Non F2P unchanged as meta weapons for the occasional opportunistic attack are probably just as relevant.
Atlas accessibility -1 -> 0 due to being added to the black market and it likely already deserved the 0-rating anyways. - Tropical
Added seeker as an option for dux. -adazahi

Aether longevity -1 -> 0, the forcefield is indeed real protection that requires concentrated firepower from several TNA titans to actually kill through. Fixed atlas being 2 on titan sheet but 3 on intro sheet. 
Murometz mobility 0 -> -1, there isn't any reason for it to have 0 in mobility when it lacks any mobility at all, unless vertical mobility is counted, but then ao ming would have 0 mobility. 
Eiffel lethality 1 ->2, having ran it myself, I feel confident in suggesting eiffel as a final bot for f2ps -Adazahi
Added Myia to Loki, Skyros, and Nightingale recommendations. -Adazahi

Added Shoggoth, Hastatus accessiblity from -1 to 0 because it is now in common data pads, Fixed Nether rating as it was different in some places, Rex lethality 0->1 due to BIW's bug fix, could even argue Rex being potential +2 lethality but that's less about a noob guide and more for power level raking -Tropical

Added shoggoth to mini build guides. May soon be worth considering Piercer to be a f2p weapon. Removed piercer from most "best builds" in favor or Shantak. Added Voonith + Urhag to the best options for most midranger builds.
Yes, I know they have longer range, but I'm not gonna make a new sniper node for every single bot that can use these op ranged guns, they work at midrange too. 
Shoggoth speed 0-> -1, bots with no mobility have -1, not 0. -Adazahi
Added Aopo as a f2p option for Anaksor. -adazahi

Skyros, Loki, nightingale Lethality -1 -> -2. Samjok lethality 0 -> -1. Loki accessibility 1 -> 2. Pathfinder and Shoggoth utility 2 -> 3. Imugi, Nuo and Lio utility 1 -> 2.
Also, Dagon was shown as -2 in the main list but actually -1 overall, so I fixed that. Jaeger, Mars, Seraph, Fury, Strider, Haechi, Bulgasari Longevity -1 -> -2, Tyr longevity 0 -> -1. Hastatus, Stryx & Ammit mobility 0 -> -1 - Adazahi
Waymaker Utility 2->3, Nether Longevity -1->-2, Nemesis Lethality 0->-1 Longevity 0 -> 1, Hawk longevity 0->-1, Pathfinder longevity 0->1. Reverted Bulgasari change. Revenant mobility 0 -> 1 lethality 0->-1, Shell & Condor utility -1 -> -2 for charging enemy nuke amps.
Changed color scheme to distinguish 3+ ratings with blue. -Mistermath

Mauler Lethality 1 -> 2; stacked up darklight is more lethal than a charged Eiffel. Newton Utility 1 -> 2; Choke is incredibly clutch and unique to Newton. 
Minos Utility -1 -> 0; Charge knocks enemies around, and CC is considered utility. Rook Utility 0 -> -1; while it has CC and suppression, it charges enemy nuclear amplifiers. 
Bedwyr Utility 1 -> 2; Taunt is an incredibly powerful and uncounterable ability that allows Bedwyr to decide the outcome of fights happening in completely different areas of the map. - Adazahi
Rex Longevity 1->0, Revenant longevity 1->0, Hastatus longevity 1->0, Ammit 2->1 utility, Teth mobility 1->0. Changes for patch. -Mistermath

Added Vulcan & Omen Vulcan, Ammit accessiblity -2 -> -1 due to now being in common data pads & Showdown becoming the new best drone for Ammit over Scales (Showdown being of course a staple F2P drone) -Tropical 
Updated mini build guides due to nerfs and added new gear. -Adazahi
Added ochokochi build guide and updated a couple others after further testing. -adazahi
Created the Titan Roles blueprint. -Tropical

Demeter longevity 0 -> 1 due to infinitely scaling heal. Fafnir utility -1 -> 1, longevity 1 -> 0 due to Webby + Noa. Dux utility -1 -> 1 due to Webby. Added fafnir build guide. Added conditional support role to Webby users -adazahi
Updated the comments for Hastatus, Rex, Mars, Pursuer, Ao Jun, Minos, Bersagliere, and Devourer (didn't actually change their ratings or point scores, just their attached comments). -Tropical
Changed how drones work for mini build guides, removing f2p drone section and listing them all in one section. Made some updates to Raptor in light of new info. -adazahi
We have issues with updating the intro page lol. Went through and fixed the ratings for ten robots that had different ratings on the intro page from what they had on the value calculator. -Adazahi
Added an automatic updater for value ratings. Now all you need to do is update the calculator and re-sort the list! -Adazahi

Skyros, Loki, Falcon Longevity 1 -> 2. Permanent uptime on incredible protection is worth the upscale. Falcon lethality & mobility 0 -> -1. We're assuming tfalc since that's far better than regular Falcon.  
Falcon access 0 -> 1 to match Skyros. T3 means cheaper upgrades, but also need to level a heavy weapon. Mender mobility 0 -> 1, Weyland mobility -2 -> 0. Buffed accelerator in support track solves problems. 
Mercury Access 0 -> 1 to match Spectre and inquisitor. Orochi Access 0 -> 1 Longevity 0 -> -1. To account for its insane downtime, I'm reducing longevity. At the same time, there's no real reason for it to have 0 accessibility.   
Khepri mobility 0 -> 1 because support track & built in speed boost, Fury longevity -2 -> -1, idk why it was so low. Bulwark longevity 1 -> 0, aegis/physical shield reliant tanks are unreliable. Siren & Leech longevity 0 ->1. 
Good uptime on reliable defenses, low base HP partially mitigated by T3 resistance passive (and/or pilots). siren utility 1 -> 0. Both siren and harpy can AoE lockdown, and freeze slowdown doesn't matter if they're locked already. 
Lynx lethality 0 -> 1. I believe execute is worth a point in lethality. Fenrir mobility -2 -> -1, Access 1 -> 0. Fenrir is a statchecker hence 0 access, and it isn't behemoth level slow hence -1 mobility. 
Phantom mobility 1 -> 2 Accessibility 1 -> 0. Phantom is a statchecker with map crossing speed and a blink back to where it started, should it so choose. -Adazahi
Reverted changes to Loki, Mercury, Orochi, Fury, Leech, Fenrir, and Phantom. Partially reverted changes to Weyland and Siren. These changes were all inconsistent with existing scores. -Mistermath
Overhauled rating system to use a 0-10 scale. -Adazahi & Mistermath

Fafnir lethality 8 -> 7. Seeing as it must pick between 2 medium + BiW and 4 medium, it probably averages 4 mediums - we can discuss later if fafnir typically gains >>2 mediums worth of charge for its BiW
Nemesis lethality 2 -> 3. I believe the BiW is worth 0.25 of a heavy or more. If the wiki is to be trusted, it has the same burst as exodus but with a far smaller total payload (~60k vs ~170k) though when charged it doubles the burst DPS and payload. 
Pursuer lethality 4 -> 2, 3 light slots with no damage boosts if I'm not missing anything. Mauler to 9 -> 10 lethality, darklight is the most lethal ability in the game bar none. Ares longevity 5 -> 6, higher uptime than 6's though lower durability to compensate
Hellburner access 7 -> 6, close range statchecker that needs levels to not instantly die (and to do damage with its explosion) Falcon utility 4 -> 2, it uses showdown over seeker, Nemesis utility 2 -> 4, it uses seeker, Nemesis access 7 -> 8, while it values bulk
slightly more than the other pantheon bots, it also only needs 2 weapons leveled. Mercury mobility 6 -> 5, it often cancels its jump partway through to dive on an enemy, thus not going as far. Cerberus longevity 4 -> 2, this thing is frailer than rayker with a 
weaker suppression. Spectre lethality 6 -> 7, 4 mediums + NA + damage boost pilot. Bulwark utility 2 -> 3, charges NA but holds seeker. Phantom utility 2 -> 4, holds seeker. 
Ao guang lethality 7 -> 6. 3M w/ NA and a far far worse BiW than ophion. Weyland utility 5 -> 7 assuming seeker, showdown isn't ideal due to how much it heals already.Weyland mobility 2 -> 3, the criterion say under 60kph w/ insufficent speed boosts. 
Weyland can reach 70kph very easily whenever it needs to, but it spends enough time slowed down to not go to the 4+ score classificiation  -adazahi
future point of discussion: Why are Siren + Harpy 6 lethality but Cerbrus 7 lethality despite having effectively the same slots + NA? Is the 20% damage pilot and BiW DoT better than Siren and Harpy BiW? Can cerberus even justify the damage pilot
with how incredibly frail it is? I am not so sure - maybe the range pilot should be assumed.

Added Piercer as a f2p option for snipers in mini build guides now that it's in weapon chest. Also added Egyptian ball family. Atlas Longevity 9 -> 8 since shields disable during jump. Waymaker lethality 8 -> 9 due to scaling potential. -Adazahi
Added Samjok mini build guide and minorly updated some drone suggestions for other guides. -Adazahi
Added some K-laser sniper builds as f2p options as well as Anaksor eldritch sniper build. -Adazahi

Reworked SWORD accessibility rating to assume players have it due to being free at one point, despite no longer being available. Edited comment section to reflect. -Mistermath
Reworked mobility rating to include vertical mobility as +1 point and reworked accessibility rating to include self exposure without adequate protection as -1 point. 
Squished all other accessibility ratings in cases where it was relevant & changed color scale to remove the light green and include more blues. -Adazahi

Added deshret+hedjet sword build and noted that it can use the sword dash but is dangerous to play. Added pulsar as an option on bots using Hazard as well as Dux. Added boom bash as shoggoth and kaji builds. -Adazahi
Tweaked the grammar and active modules which robots should use in the Mini Build Guides -Tropical
Added Kroko builds to absorber bots and Kaji. -Adazahi
Changed Fujin from B tier to S tier on the Camelot tier list to reflect its new Aegis shield change. -Mistermath

Added Fang & Sirocco, adjusted accessiblity ratings of Anaksor 1 -> 4 and Princeps 1 -> 3 -Tropical
Updated mini build guides to include new gear -Adazahi
Removed extraneous commentary about Sirocco to keep text within 1 line. -Mistermath
Anaksor accessibility 4 -> 3 due to overreliance on Myia -Adazahi

Princeps access 3 -> 8 since it's in black market and a non-statchecker. Waymaker access 1 -> 3 since it's in normal titan pad. Rook access 5 -> 4, Mauler access 3 -> 4, these bots will be treated as assassins rather than straight up statcheckers. -Adazahi
Hastatus Longevity 5 -> 7 Lethality 7 -> 8. Hastatus was underrated in these categories; its BIW and defensive ability were both getting underrated. -Adazahi

Fang accessibility 0 -> 1, accounting for high stealth uptime, speed, and useful utility. -Mistermath
Shenlou longevity 5 -> 4, it was a bit overrated compared to the other 5's -Adazahi
Added seeker as an option for Loki due to countersuppression. -Adazahi

Vector Mobility 10 -> 8, Vector Longevity 10 -> 8. After Vector's nerf, it will be comparable to Raptor in the sense that it has good burst mobility with insane downtime issues as the match goes on. 
Since the reflector is being removed from the speed part of the ability, you will need to spam cancel at close quarters in order to get the reflector back, eating your charges and preventing you from spending as much time moving as you'd like. -Adazahi

Added UE bot value ratings and mini build guides.
Mender mobility 8 -> 7. Mender does not reach its theoretical maximum speed due to a low speed cap. -Adazahi

Added UE Titan roles to all titan roles (deleted the separate tab that Tropical made), added UE Titan value ratings to all titan value rating tab, added UE bots to mini build guides.
Ao Ming mobility 4 -> 5. This doesn't really matter for Ming much as it is T2 and thus bad, but I never noticed that Ming's mobility was this low and I don't really agree with it, so it needs to be changed for normal ming
in order to have parity with UE Ming. UE Ming is 7 rather than 5 due to speed boosts from specializations and speed boost on heal as a UE trait. The majority of the reasoning for this change is just because of the
value of Ming's vertical mobility. While it isn't very fast in the sense that it can cross long distances, it can fly over obstacles and access cover that most bots cannot. The flight having a 5 second cooldown and infinite
duration is why it is notably higher mobility of other flying titans.
Adjusted lethality scores for Kid, Arthur, and Ao Ming to treat them as though they are simply TNAless titans (ie Ao Ming firepower = Bjorn firepower)
Luchador mobility 2 -> 4 to match with Bjorn. Bjorn accessibility 3 -> 2 to match with luchador. Aether mobility 5 -> 6, spamming the dashes in air can make it actually somewhat quick. 
Arthur mobility 1 -> 0 Kid and sharanga mobility 2 -> 1 Devourer mobility 3 -> 2 Sharanga mobility 1 -> 2 Bedwyr and newton mobility 2 -> 3
Redefined lethality for titans. Most high lethality titan ratings haven't changed at all, though lower lethality titans have dropped by about 1 point across the board. Sirocco utility 8 -> 9 because rust EMP field is mega broken
-Adazahi

Nuo is probably the only bot in the game that can make a f2p friendly sniper build. Since it gives itself

not worth spending memorium on Basil since he's so incredibly niche, and sometimes there
is a friendly sniper in the backline with you that makes great use of the link. Harold is ideal
for K-lasers though. For weapons without built in defense mitigation, Solar becomes the best drone.
Solar still works with railguns, but its value is questionable.

builds.explanation:
UE Fenrir is an incredibly annoying to kill tank that can abuse Showdown's healing due to its grey resistance. It is
unfortunately hard countered by rust and percentage damage, which can cripple it incredibly quickly.

robots.name: Harpy
robots.comments: Harpy's BiW blast effect provides a decent chunk of damage, but the weaker reflector holds it back from ever being in competetion with Siren.

robots.name: Siren
robots.comments: Between the twin fliers, Siren's freeze and stronger reflector give it a notable edge in overall power. Equipped with lockdown unit, it can immobilize an entire team with its snowstorm.

robots.name: Typhon
robots.comments: Typhon's access to mid-range support, availability in the super chest, and high damage make it a solid option. However, it is seriously outclassed by Pathfinder.

robots.name: Orochi
robots.comments: Orochi's multiple dashes with stealth are decent in a vacuum, but are also competing with Lynx and Raven.

robots.name: Demeter
robots.comments: Demeter's ability has possibly the strongest healing in the entire game, though on a moderate CD. Even at level 1, the absorber shield can be hugely impactful, deciding the outcome of duels in seconds.

robots.name: Jaeger
robots.comments: Jaeger is worse than Fury.

robots.name: Scorpion
robots.comments: Scorpion is good for picking off weakened or vulnerable enemies, even without much investment.

robots.name: Erebus
robots.comments: Erebus, similarly to Typhon, has solid mid-range support and excellent damage.

robots.name: Fafnir
robots.comments: While half-reliance on defense points and half reliance on absorber to stay alive is unappealing, Fafnir's damage potential and webby synergy make up for it.

robots.name: Hawk
robots.comments: Compared to the other aerial bots, Hawk lacks both damage and utility. The retraction of weapons during flight hurts it terribly, so it should fly as little as possible (only to escape bad positions) and play as Natasha Pro Max.

robots.name: Nightingale
robots.comments: A true support, Nightingale provides long-lasting healing and protection via its suppression effect at the cost of any offensive capacity.

robots.name: Ravana
robots.comments: Ravana is accessible, threatening, and nearly impossible to kill when Transcendance is used properly.

robots.name: Shell
robots.comments: Shell is a less accessible version of Hellburner that also runs the risk of charging opposing Nuclear Amplifiers.

robots.name: Khepri
robots.comments: Khepri has a solid mix of supporting and offensive capabilities, limited mainly by how modest both its base stats and its bonuses are individually.

robots.name: Revenant
robots.comments: Revenant's protection from grey damage necessitates tons of healing to make useful, which means lots of investment and a giant powercell burn rate. However, with Ricardo + Engine Expert, Revenant becomes extremely fast on top of already being able to teleport.

robots.name: Skyros
robots.comments: Skyros is an F2P beacon capturing machine, not even requiring a single upgrade or any equipment to work. It competes with Loki, whose stealth is sometimes superior to Skyros's resistances.

robots.name: Seraph
robots.comments: Seraph technically has a niche via stellar air speed, but is otherwise unremarkable. It's alright for mindlessly clearing early PvE levels.

robots.name: Mars
robots.comments: Mars is heavily reliant on its turret to differentiate itself, but the slow projectile speed and outright mediocre damage means it's unfortunately unreliable.

robots.name: Angler
robots.comments: Angler can provide minor team support and is somewhat hard to kill, but is also a slow tank.

robots.name: Nether
robots.comments: Nether's a decent beacon runner or suicide lead, but Imugi, Skyros, Loki, Raptor, and Teth all do the job better.

robots.name: Imugi
robots.comments: The cycle of stealth, healing, teleport+healing, repeat makes Imugi extremely powerful. With its availability in the workshop, it's one of the best F2P bots in the game.

robots.name: Lynx
robots.comments: Lynx's defensive tools in stealth and forcefield both don't care about level. That combined with the execute gun and high speed make Lynx a solid and accessible hit-and-run damage dealer.

robots.name: Crisis
robots.comments: Near permanent stealth and long-range camping make Crisis a fairly safe sniper, but also can make it a liability on short maps with clumped beacons.

robots.name: Ophion
robots.comments: Ophion's built-in-weapon has only 350m range, forcing you to play on a knife's edge with the absorber.

robots.name: Ochokochi
robots.comments: Compared to Fenrir, Ocho does have some utility and mobility, but is similarly hard to invest in. It's best saved for the few maps where it can knock people off edges.

robots.name: Dagon
robots.comments: Dagon is moderately powerful but difficult to invest in, given its stat-check nature and 6 hardpoints.

robots.name: Curie
robots.comments: Curie's an all-around decent bot, but is short-ranged and thus a less reliable lockdown source than Typhon, Erebus, Siren, or Pathfinder.

robots.name: Shenlou
robots.comments: Shenlou is reliant on its dome Aegis for protection, which causes it to get into more stat-checking scenarios than Scorpion's stealth.

robots.name: Pathfinder
robots.comments: Pathfinder's performance remains incredible across all investment levels; between speed boosts, damage boosts, lockdown, shieldbreak, healing, and more, it can truly do it all.

robots.name: Raptor
robots.comments: Raptor's jumps provide it with just enough flexibility to act as an off-tank beacon runner in a role similar to Leech or Teth.

robots.name: Bagliore
robots.comments: Bagliore hits harder than Crisis, is bulkier, and has a teleport, but has no stealth, power stored in a MK3 upgrade, and no built-in shieldbreaker.

robots.name: Condor
robots.comments: Condor's a mediore statchecker with no notable traits that'd make it worth investing into.

robots.name: Dux
robots.comments: Dux has high damage output and decent survivability, making it a solid tank-buster similar to Lynx. It can also wield Webby, further enhancing its ability to tank bust.

robots.name: Ravager
robots.comments: Ravager is functionally a bulkier Crisis without the shieldbreaker. However, 5 hardpoints make it hard to invest in. It can alternatively be a slower Loki.

robots.name: Samjok
robots.comments: Samjok is easier to take down between phases compared to ravana. The turret is still deadly, even post nerf, though phase uptime is severely limited.

robots.name: Nuo
robots.comments: Nuo's damage and teammate-buffing abilities are strong. Though not listed ingame, it also gets tremendous in-flight speed.

robots.name: Lio
robots.comments: Lio's bulk and teammate-buffing abilities are strong.

robots.name: Sword Unit
robots.comments: A level 1 Sword with level 1 ARMs equipped is a genuinely viable tankbuster, making it a solid F2P choice. Lockdown Unit or Ward are great ways to keep a tank in place and soften them up for your teammates. Unfortunately it's a collab item that is no longer obtainable.

robots.name: Teth
robots.comments: Teth's EMP is good utility, making it comparable to Raptor as a tank but with much less mobility.

robots.name: Stryx
robots.comments: Stryx has incredibly high fire power. However, 5 hard points make it difficult to invest in.

robots.name: Kaji
robots.comments: Kaji is a strategic minelayer with the potential to tear high health & slower enemies apart. It doesn't rely on its weapons much, having high damage potential with the mines alone in most cases.

robots.name: Rex
robots.comments: Rex is the second coming of Ochokochi. Very strong, but a bit difficult to invest in. Aside from being a twice nerfed brawler robot and thus increasingly susceptible to newer releases, it suffers if not mk3 and outfitted with more complete features (drone, pilot, etc).

robots.name: Hastatus
robots.comments: Hastatus is a versatile midranger with a decent defense system that can be best described as "Phase shift but you can shoot." Effective but somewhat difficult to invest in, requiring mk3 for maximum efficiency, and is counterplayed pretty easily.

robots.name: Ammit
robots.comments: Ammit does too much. It has the ability of a glass cannon with the stats of a tank, all while passively applying negative effects to anyone nearby. While it's already OP at base, it can be even further improved, as investing in this robot makes it pretty much gamebreaking.

robots.name: Anaksor
robots.comments: Anaksor is an exceptional assassin and tank-buster. Utility, mobility, and evasiveness make it great even when just MK2'd.

robots.name: Vector
robots.comments: Vector is a modern cross between an Ochokochi and a Raptor: It has immense survivability, crowd control that can toss enemies out of bounds, and map-crossing speed. Unfortunately, like most new brawlers, it requires mk3 at minimum for maximum impact.

robots.name: Shoggoth
robots.comments: It was hard to believe that pixonic would powercreep Pathfinder, but you truly can't underestimate their motives to add the most unhealthy robots to the game as possible. Shoggoth is an unholy abomination child between mother Pathfinder and father Bagliore.

robots.name: Vulcan
robots.comments: Vulcan is the next generation of damage dealers, quite literally a walking Nuclear Amplifier: effortless to scale up, incredibly lethal, strong defensive capabilities for a non-brawling robot, and haunting strength if you obtain its special edition variant and equip Webby...

robots.name: Omen Vulcan
robots.comments: Vulcan is a one of a kind robot that requires two seperate entries in order to reveal its actual value; the Special Edition Vulcan causes Webby to apply 100% rust permanently against any targets you aim at. Exceedingly lethal to use against brawler/healing reliant titans.

robots.name: Fang
robots.comments: Fang is a potent assassin that single handedly dismantles Vectors and other brawlers alike. Rusts and EMPs through walls, can hit multiple targets at the same time, as is now the fastest robot in the game.

robots.name: Fury
robots.comments: Fury has decent firepower, comes pre-leveled, and its pilot grants it access to unlimited shieldbreaker. It's a barely passable sniper to use as a weapon platform while you wait for something better.

robots.name: Strider
robots.comments: Strider has some potential with the legendary pilot, but it is too outclassed by Nether.

robots.name: Raven
robots.comments: Raven is the gold standard for offensive F2P bots, staying viable all the way up in champion league via its legendary pilot.

robots.name: Rayker
robots.comments: Rayker's long-range support ability makes it a tenable contributor to a team, even with no investment.

robots.name: Ao Guang
robots.comments: Ao Guang is mediocre in the air and terrible outside of it.

robots.name: Bulgasari
robots.comments: Bulgasari is mediocre to bad across the board, and really needs its legendary pilot to function at all.

robots.name: Hellburner
robots.comments: With the legendary pilot, Hellburner gains a bit of extra survivability, but it is limited by low base durability and terrible hardpoints.

robots.name: Cerberus
robots.comments: Cerberus's utility via Blackout is seriously limited by its low range and lack of an EMP.

robots.name: Haechi
robots.comments: Haechi is similar to Bulgasari, but also lacks a decent pilot.

robots.name: Inquisitor
robots.comments: Inquisitor does a decent Raven impression early on, but once Raven gets its legendary pilot, Inquisitor is strictly worse.

robots.name: Falcon
robots.comments: T-falcon is very cheap and tanky, but not nearly as good as modern brawlers. Regular Falcon isn't worth playing.

robots.name: Pursuer
robots.comments: The existence of Loki means that Pursuer needs to make use of its ability to fire while stealthed. Unfortunately, 3 lights, no dash, and long ability cooldown means it can't reliably assassinate.

robots.name: Spectre
robots.comments: Spectre is one of multiple Inquisitor sidegrades that all fall short of Raven. 4M makes it the best sidegrade, but still not good enough.

robots.name: Mercury
robots.comments: Mercury is a sidegrade to Inquisitor, trading hardpoint strength for a better ability.

robots.name: Nemesis
robots.comments: Nemesis sacrifices too much firepower and speed for its absorber shield.

robots.name: Weyland
robots.comments: Weyland is a relatively slow close-range support-tank hybrid, necessitating heavy investment for not questionable return.

robots.name: Behemoth
robots.comments: Behemoth's worse than Bagliore in basically every way. Even Fury has a niche over it with its shieldbreaker.

robots.name: Bulwark
robots.comments: Bulwark is a statcheck machine that loses to other statcheck machines.

robots.name: Invader
robots.comments: Invader's biggest issue is that as a statchecking tank, you'll need to upgrade it tremendously before it will have enough durability to do its job.

robots.name: Mender
robots.comments: Mender is a more mobile version of Weyland that has the ability to heal a minor amount of grey damage through its legendary pilot.

robots.name: Loki
robots.comments: Loki's blazing fast speed and permanent stealth make it an excellent beacon runner, even with no investment required.

robots.name: Tyr
robots.comments: Tyr's an unimpressive middle ground between Weyland's bulk and Mender's speed.

robots.name: Blitz
robots.comments: Blitz plays a lot like Hellburner, but has the added bonuses of a longer ability and access to suppression.

robots.name: Fenrir
robots.comments: Fenrir is a strange case. It's given for free and can use midrange weapons somewhat well, but reaching Fenrir's maximum potential as a closerange statchecker requires tons of investment.

robots.name: Hades
robots.comments: Hades is better than Nemesis, but is still plainly outclassed by other absorber bots.

robots.name: Ao Jun
robots.comments: Ao Jun is frail and requires getting extremely close in order to use its flamethrowers, making it too risky for not much reward. Its long cooldown and generally short lived playstyle makes it extremely clunky to use, especially in comparison to other flying bots.

robots.name: Ares
robots.comments: With high damage, Ares has the power to accomplish a decent amount during its absorber uptime.

robots.name: Leech
robots.comments: Leech is a huge threat on the battlefield with proper positioning and timing of its ability. After its shift from T4 to T3, it's also extremely accessible.

robots.name: Phantom
robots.comments: Phantom is essentially a Loki with brawling tendencies. Few bots are both as fast and tanky as it is; though it pays for it in the firepower department.

robots.name: UE Ao Jun
robots.comments: UE Ao Jun is one of the weaker UE bots in the game, though if you manage to get your hands on one, it is nonetheless a competent raider.

robots.name: UE Ares
robots.comments: UE Ares is a fairly old UE and it shows, though it still holds up as an acceptable damage dealer if you manage to obtain it.

robots.name: UE Blitz
robots.comments: UE Blitz is an exceptionally fast saboteur with some added utility in the form of suppression that can aid it in making aggressive plays.

robots.name: UE Bulgasari
robots.comments: UE Bulgasari is incredibly mobile, though it isn't particularly bulky nor capable of particularly high damage. If you can make use of the unbreakable shield, you can be really annoying to enemies without splash.

robots.name: UE Destrier
robots.comments: UE Destrier was given for free on anniversary, and as well all know, in War Robots, you get what you (don't) pay for.

robots.name: UE Fenrir
robots.comments: UE Fenrir is incredibly tanky but practically immobile and offers no utility.

robots.name: UE Fujin
robots.comments: UE Fuijin is a victim of its own specialization: For some reason it was given Brawler rather than Damage Dealer, which isn't particularly helpful for a low HP bot that relies on its shield.

robots.name: UE Griffin
robots.comments: UE Griffin can apply blind to a lot of enemies at once, which is annoying, but it doesn't last all too long. During the cooldown of blind, Griffin is left with little to defend itself with.

robots.name: UE Haechi
robots.comments: UE Haechi is notoriously difficult to kill without shieldbreaker, as it can have incredibly high uptime on its flexible absorber charges.

robots.name: UE Hawk
robots.comments: UE Hawk suffers from chip damage, though unlike normal Hawk, its firepower is dangerous both in air and on the ground.

robots.name: UE Invader
robots.comments: UE Invader is a poor tank, not just by UE standards, but also by regular bot standards. It lacks any the protection systems required to properly brawl with meta tanks.

robots.name: UE Lancelot
robots.comments: UE Lancelot unfortunately is a nuclear amplifier charger, but that is really its only big weakness. It is both mobile, tanky, and posesses plenty of self sustaining grey repair.

robots.name: UE Leech
robots.comments: UE Leech is not a significant upgrade over normal Leech, but normal Leech is pretty good, so UE Leech is pretty good too.

robots.name: UE Leo
robots.comments: UE Leo is a Bagliore-esque Brawler/Damage Dealer hybrid, ditching the fancy tricks of traditional damage dealers for a fairly high health pool and reflector. It also has easy access to both QS (pilot) and SB (Hawkeye) allowing it to counter many bots at once.

robots.name: UE Mender
robots.comments: UE Mender is held back by its awful firepower. Nonetheless, it is moderately tanky and fairly fast, plus it can grey heal teammates.

robots.name: UE Phantom
robots.comments: UE Phantom is incredibly fast and fairly tanky, plus its firepower isn't nearly as bad as normal Phantom. Still, it is susceptable to being bursted down, especially when outside of ability.

robots.name: UE Ravana
robots.comments: UE Ravana leans into all the things that made the original Ravana good and improves on them, making for a very powerful ultimate brawler.

robots.name: UE Raven
robots.comments: UE Raven is completely broken, able to stack stealth, stasis barrier, and incredible grey healing from Scourveil into one dangerous, high firepower package.

robots.name: UE Rayker
robots.comments: UE Rayker is like a Pathfinder without the Hunter Marks... which is, fine, I guess? Hunter is what makes Pathfinder so OP, but everything else about Pathfinder is also OP, so Rayker is pretty good. Plus, it can execute!

robots.name: UE Revenant
robots.comments: UE Revenant is an incredibly powerful self sustaining brawler with two unbreakable shields and a long distance teleport. Ricardo makes UE Revenant incredibly mobile when used with Engine Expert, though Revenant gives up a lot of firepower for its tankieness.

robots.name: UE Rhino
robots.comments: UE Rhino is potentially the tankiest bot in the game, becoming virtually unkillable while in ability. Unfortunately, it gives up on a lot of firepower to accomplish this.

robots.name: UE Sword Unit
robots.comments: UE Sword has massive damage potential with its sword, assuming you can fool an enemy into charging you up. Aside from that, it is not all too different from regular sword.

robots.name: UE Scorpion
robots.comments: UE Scorpion is a cross between a saboteur and a brawler, able to get in, bite the ankles of something way out of its weight class, and then get out just as fast.

robots.name: UE Spectre
robots.comments: UE Spectre is a sidegrade to regular edition raven, having better firepower but worse everything else.

robots.name: UE Typhon
robots.comments: UE Typhon's blackout and firepower make it insanely dangerous, though it is fairly frail and its long cooldown leaves it open to be punished if it makes a mistake.

titans.name: Kid
titans.comments: Kid is given for free. It's only worth using until you get any other titan to replace it with.

titans.name: Arthur
titans.comments: T2 titans are not worth wasting platinum on. Their lack of specializations neuters their stats.

titans.name: Ao Ming
titans.comments: T2 titans are not worth wasting platinum on. Their lack of specializations neuters their stats.

titans.name: Nodens
titans.comments: Nodens is a cheap, simple, and reasonably effective support. The increased defense mitigation it has on its passive makes it no slouch on offense despite having only beta weapons.

titans.name: Minos
titans.comments: Minos is a fast, safe, and cheap beacon runner and brawler, though it's less effective at killing enemy titans then most due to its lack of Alpha hardpoints.

titans.name: Sharanga
titans.comments: Sharanga is an offensive titan without the proper tools to stay safe or gain target access.

titans.name: Murometz
titans.comments: Murometz can often straight-up kill opposing titans while they are EMP'd by it, making it a solid, cheap anti-titan titan.

titans.name: Luchador
titans.comments: Luchador is one of the weaker brawling titans, making it a statchecker that is bad at statchecking.

titans.name: Heimdall
titans.comments: Heimdall has decent supporting capacity, though its extra cost over Nodens comes with questionable benefit.

titans.name: Indra
titans.comments: Like Ravana, Indra's phasing and lasso scale with the opponent's strength, making it an excellent anti-meta choice.

titans.name: Aether
titans.comments: Aether is to Murometz what Heimdall is to Nodens. More expensive with questionable sidegrades.

titans.name: Sirius
titans.comments: With a giant hitbox, poor speed, and miniscule damage, Sirius is a sitting duck.

titans.name: Rook
titans.comments: Rook's huge dash lets it play the role of an assassin or beacon runner, though it does the job very unreliably and lacks good survival tools.

titans.name: Newton
titans.comments: Newton's a solid sniper whose choke provides good team utility.

titans.name: Eiffel
titans.comments: If you can afford to build it by acquiring weapons for and leveling the required 5 hardpoints, Eiffel has unmatched raw firepower. Hybrid setups using instant unload snipers (ie Vendicatoire) in the summoned slots are recommended.

titans.name: Bedwyr
titans.comments: Bedwyr's taunt and giant absorber provide great team support and survivability that doesn't depend solely on stats, respectively.

titans.name: Bersagliere
titans.comments: Between stealth, 3 Alphas, persistent shieldbreaker, and a large jump, Bersagliere has all the tools it needs to be a strong and safe damage dealer.

titans.name: Mauler
titans.comments: Mauler is extremely deadly, and enemies in its abillity's zone will melt rapidly. However, without significant investment, it will be frail for a long time.

titans.name: Devourer
titans.comments: Devourer is a debuffer that can seriously impede enemies' movement, damage, and defense by essence shifting them. Unfortunately, it relies on allies or mothership effects in order to make use of this ability as it is susceptible to being bursted down.

titans.name: Bjorn
titans.comments: Bjorn is a decent statchecker with high uptime and firepower but poor mobility outside of ball mode. It trades luchador's jump for it's better ability uptime and an extra alpha weapon.

titans.name: Atlas
titans.comments: Atlas is comparable to Bedwyr, namely trading off Taunt and a more utility focused absorber shield for nasty EMP application & area denial, plus some mobility.

titans.name: Princeps
titans.comments: Princeps has an overpowered mix of high damage, the best defensive ability in the game, and as a cherry on top, crowd control utility. Since it is now available in the black market, it's far more obtainable for f2p players, though it is definitely at risk of getting nerfed soon.

titans.name: Waymaker
titans.comments: Waymaker is a potent support titan that's dragged down by the rest of its kit. It also suffers from opportunity cost; pathfinder & shoggoth only require a robot slot to do what they do while waymaker requires a titan slot.

titans.name: Sirocco
titans.comments: Sirocco has Indra's evergreen feature of going into phase while also being extremely mobile and durable. This is combined with a utility perk similar to Atlas' with potent rust and EMP.

titans.name: UE Ao Ming
titans.comments: Assumes UE TNA. Ming is pretty much the fattest statchecker in the game with massive firepower and decent longevity to back it up. If played with UE TRA, it can competently fend off enemy brawlers as well as bully enemy damage dealers.

titans.name: UE Arthur
titans.comments: Assumes UE TNA. UE Arthur is not nearly tanky enough to make use of UE TRA. While it is a massive pain to deal with if you don't have splash damage, it is a free kill if you do.

titans.name: UE Murometz
titans.comments: Assumes UE TNA. UE Murometz is currently one of the strongest titans in the game. Its EMP is dangerous, it has insane self sustaining grey heals, and the stealth has incredibly high uptime. UE TRA can be used as a get out of jail free card that lowers your ceiling output.

titans.name: UE Nodens
titans.comments: Assumes UE TRA. Both a powerful grey healing and speed boosting support and a staller that is difficult to take down without rust, the assistance UE Nodens is always appreciated on the team.

titans.name: UE Minos
titans.comments: Assumes UE TRA. UE Minos is a tanky staller that is very similar to the original one. The biggest upgrade you'll notice is the incredibly long duration EMP that its charge applies.
